web_title: 0. Executive Thesis, Dual Verdict & Opportunity Matrix
book_title: Prologue: The Business, The Price & Our Independent Verdict
question: Is NIKE's 45% drawdown a generational entry into an iconic consumer compounder, or an expensive 25.5x forward-P/E turnaround still fighting China contraction and broken technicals?

epigraph.quote: Great brands survive self-inflicted strategic detours, but shareholders only compound when they buy the turn at an asymmetric price—never on brand nostalgia alone.
epigraph.author: Research Desk Underwriting Charter

web_blocks.html: NIKE Inc (NYSE: NKE) is the world's largest athletic footwear and apparel company ($46.40B FY2026 revenue; 73,000 employees) [2, 23]. Under CEO Elliott Hill's "Win Now" reset, NIKE is unwinding its 2020–2023 direct-to-consumer overreach, repairing ties with Dick's Sporting Goods and Foot Locker, and refocusing on performance running [3]. Early green shoots appeared in North America wholesale (+9% in Q1 FY2027), yet Greater China (-26% CC), NIKE Direct (-8%), Converse (-28%), and FCF ($2.18B vs. $2.41B dividend) remain under pressure [2, 3]. At Friday's November 13, 2026 close of $37.99 ($56.43B market cap; 25.54x Forward P/E), we assign WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT (`TIER_3` Watchlist) for new capital and HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP for the existing 74.5773 shares ($2,833.19; 3.19% weight) in Robinhood [23, 29].

web_blocks.title: Why Patience Pays: Valuation, Peers & Technical Gate
paragraphs: Our Reverse DCF shows $37.99 already prices in a 3.5% ten-year revenue CAGR and an 11.5% terminal operating margin [2, 23]. Shares also sit -15.18% below a declining 200-day moving average ($44.79) in a US market Correction [23, 29]. At $37.99, reward-to-risk is only 0.85:1 to our $43.50 base target against a $31.50 stop.

Peer comparisons sharpen this discipline. Competitors Deckers (10.69x forward P/E, 38.11% ROIC) and On Holding (16.47x forward P/E, +24.02% TTM sales growth) trade at lower forward multiples with stronger margins [23, 25, 26]. Even Lululemon trades at 12.61x forward P/E [23, 27]. Paying 25.54x forward earnings for NKE today leaves no margin of safety. Instead, we hold 100% of marginal capital in USD cash and set alerts for either $33.50–$35.00 support (2.43:1 R:R) or a confirmed Stage 2 reclaim above $40.77–$44.79 [29]. Both our options and equity desks agree on waiting patiently for asymmetric confirmation before committing any fresh capital to this turnaround. Until then, T-bills pay us to wait.

book_paragraphs: Every great brand eventually tests its investors' discipline. NIKE, Inc.—a $46.40 billion global juggernaut whose Swoosh is recognized in every corner of the planet—has fallen 45% from its 52-week high to $37.99 as of November 13, 2026. To a casual shopper, a 45% sale on a Dow 30 icon looks like an automatic buy. To a disciplined institutional underwriter, price without forensic context is a siren song.

That is why you and I built this monograph in two strict, sealed passes. In Chapters 1 through 6, we locked the ticker tape in a drawer and examined NIKE purely as a business: its sixty-year history, its four geographic engines, its Vietnam-and-Indonesia contract manufacturing spine, its competitive fight with On, HOKA, and Adidas, and ten years of cash-flow forensics. That price-blind audit earned NIKE a CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL / PASS_WITH_WATCH grade—a resilient net-cash franchise showing early North America wholesale stabilization (+9%), yet still bleeding in Greater China (-26% CC), NIKE Direct (-8%), and Converse (-28%), with free cash flow ($2.18B) trailing its $2.41B dividend.

In Chapters 7 through 9, we unlocked the market price ($37.99), ran a Reverse DCF, benchmarked NIKE against Deckers, On Holding, and Lululemon, and read the weekly chart. The verdict is clear: WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT (TIER_3 Watchlist) for new capital, and HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP on our existing 74.5773 shares in Robinhood ($2,850.00 cost basis, $2,833.19 market value, 3.19% portfolio weight). At $37.99, new money faces 25.54x forward earnings with only 0.85:1 reward-to-risk to our $43.50 base target. We keep 100% of marginal cash in T-bills today, protect the existing Robinhood shares with a hard $31.50 stop, and wait for either a $33.50–$35.00 support test backed by Dec 17 fundamental confirmation or a Stage 2 volume breakout above $40.77–$44.79.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Our job is not to predict when NIKE will become cool again—it is to demand a price where the math pays us generously for waiting, or wait for the chart to prove institutions agree.

book_subsections.title: How to Use This Monograph Across Horizons
paragraphs: Before we dive into Chapter 1, let's align on how to read this two-part dossier. If you are a short-term momentum trader looking for a one-to-twelve-week swing, Chapter 8 gives you the clear answer: stand aside, because a stock trading 15.2% below its 200-day moving average on 0.37x relative volume in a Correction regime has no momentum edge.

If you are a medium-term inflection or long-term compounding investor, Chapters 2 through 7 give you the exact operational scorecard: North America wholesale (+9%) is healing, but Greater China (-26% CC), NIKE Direct (-8%), and free cash flow ($2.18B vs. $2.41B dividend) have not turned yet. Keep your cash earning T-bill yields today, set alerts at $33.50–$35.00 support and $40.77–$44.79 Stage 2 reclaim, and let price and fundamentals confirm the turn. Above all, resist the urge to anchor on a 52-week high of $69.14; in institutional turnarounds, what matters is forward cash generation, not where the stock used to trade.
